artifacts.title: Big Picture: The September 2026 Frontier AI Convergence

claims: Convergence on RLVR and programmatic verifiers replaced subjective RLHF
Dynamic test-time compute allows models to search and self-correct across up to 256K thinking tokens
Sparse MoE scaled to 2.4T-2.8T total parameters while keeping active compute sub-90B
Agent-native environment training optimized tool economy (Muse 1.3 20% fewer tool calls) alongside 75% cheaper prompt caching
Synthetic verification flywheels enable rapid distillation into high-speed workhorse models like Gemini 3.8 Flash in 3-week cycles
functions: Interactive Frontier Capability & Breakthrough Ablation Simulator
5-Model Deep Dive Matrix (Google, Meta, Alibaba, Anthropic, Moonshot AI)
observable_effects: Toggling individual breakthrough mechanisms dynamically updates projected reasoning capability, latency, and token cost in the simulator
Selecting individual models updates the architecture specs, context window, and pricing metrics
Step-by-step pipeline walkthrough visually traces the transition from pretraining to inference search and distillation

rules: Ground all claims in verified September 2026 release data and research papers
Explicitly distinguish empirical facts from illustrative browser simulation projections
Expose invalidation conditions and boundary limitations

objective: Explain why frontier AI models (Gemini 3.8, Muse Spark 1.3, Qwen3.8-Max 0902, Claude Fable 5.1, Kimi K3) leaped forward simultaneously in September 2026 by synthesizing the 5 technological breakthroughs driving cross-lab convergence.
audience: Technical leaders, AI researchers, software architects, and engineering teams
